crisis.name: Submarine Landslide Shock
crisis.effectText: A huge undersea landslide buries seafloor communities in mud. Remove bottom-dwelling organisms in deep-sea and slope biomes.

crisis.name: Pumice Raft Drift
crisis.effectText: A volcanic eruption sends floating pumice rafts across the sea, shading waters and clogging coasts. Remove surface-feeding organisms from gyres and shoreline spaces.

crisis.name: Kelp Forest Collapse
crisis.effectText: A rare warm current and urchin boom wipe out kelp forests. Remove kelp and shelter-loving species from temperate rocky coasts.

crisis.name: Warm Current Coral Stress
crisis.effectText: A strong natural warm current lingers over reef zones. Remove coral-building organisms in shallow tropical reef spaces.
biomesGood: Marine (Tropical Upwelling, Temperate Shelf and Seas)

crisis.name: Bark Beetle Explosion
crisis.effectText: Mild winters let bark beetles explode in number. Remove pine and spruce trees heavily attacked by beetles.
biomesBad: Forest (Temperate Coniferous Forests, Boreal Forests and Taiga)

crisis.name: Understory Fire Storm
crisis.effectText: Lightning ignites fires that race through the forest floor. Remove leaf-litter decomposers and understory plants.
biomesBad: Forest (Tropical and Subtropical Moist Broadleaf Forests, Temperate Broadleaf and Mixed Forests)
biomesGood: Forest (Mediterranean Forests, Woodlands, and Scrub, Temperate Coniferous Forests)

crisis.name: Windthrow Patchwork
crisis.effectText: A mega-storm knocks down swaths of trees, opening the canopy. Remove large trees in selected forest spaces and treat them as fresh gaps.
biomesBad: Forest (Temperate Broadleaf and Mixed Forests, Tropical and Subtropical Moist Broadleaf Forests)
biomesGood: Forest (Montane Grasslands and Shrublands, Mediterranean Forests, Woodlands, and Scrub)

crisis.name: Canopy Ice Breakage
crisis.effectText: A heavy ice storm coats branches until they snap. Remove canopy trees and high-branch species in affected forests.

crisis.name: Sand Dune Encroachment
crisis.effectText: Winds push dunes over nearby habitats, burying soils and roots. Remove organisms in advancing dune and desert edge spaces.
biomesBad: Desert (Deserts and Xeric Shrublands, Xeric Basins)

crisis.name: Flash Drought Heat Spike
crisis.effectText: A sudden, brutal heat wave hits even hardy desert life. Remove less-tolerant plants and animals from exposed desert spaces.
biomesBad: Desert (Deserts and Xeric Shrublands, Xeric Basins)

crisis.name: Dust Storm Season
crisis.effectText: Choking dust clouds block sun and coat leaves. Remove small plants and air-breathers in chosen desert and downwind grassland spaces.

crisis.name: Native Herbivore Surge
crisis.effectText: Native herbivore herds crowd the desert fringe after a few good years. Remove palatable grasses and small plants from margin grassland spaces.
biomesBad: Grassland (Tropical and Subtropical Grasslands, Savannas, and Shrublands)

crisis.name: Locust Swarm Year
crisis.effectText: Shifting rains trigger huge locust swarms that strip grasses and herbs. Remove plant producers from affected grassland spaces.
biomesBad: Grassland (Tropical and Subtropical Grasslands, Savannas, and Shrublands, Temperate Grasslands, Savannas, and Shrublands)
biomesGood: Grassland (Flooded Grasslands and Savannas, Montane Grasslands and Shrublands)

crisis.name: Mega-Herbivore Crash
crisis.effectText: Disease and harsh seasons wipe out large grazers. Remove big herbivore tokens and let woody plants begin to invade.

crisis.name: Unseasonal Frost on Plains
crisis.effectText: A surprise frost hits during growing or nesting season. Remove young plants and nests from selected grassland spaces.
biomesBad: Grassland (Temperate Grasslands, Savannas, and Shrublands, Montane Grasslands and Shrublands)

crisis.name: Ash-Fall Grassland Mantle
crisis.effectText: Distant volcanoes dust grasslands with ash. Remove delicate plants in freshly ash-covered spaces; later these soils may hold more water and nutrients.
biomesGood: Grassland (Montane Grasslands and Shrublands, Flooded Grasslands and Savannas)

crisis.name: Permafrost Thaw Slump
crisis.effectText: Frozen ground melts and collapses into muddy slumps. Remove tundra plants and soil animals from thawed hill and riverbank spaces; some form new ponds.

crisis.name: Snowpack Failure Winter
crisis.effectText: Thin, icy snow no longer protects tundra life. Remove small animals and plants that rely on soft snow cover.

crisis.name: Ice-Algae Collapse
crisis.effectText: A rare warm-water intrusion melts seasonal sea ice early. Remove ice-dependent producers and animals from polar marine spaces.
biomesGood: Marine (Temperate Shelf and Seas, Temperate Upwelling)

crisis.name: Tundra Shrub Takeover
crisis.effectText: A natural warm phase lets shrubs spread over open tundra. Replace low tundra plants and open-ground species with taller shrubs and new browsers.

crisis.name: Peatland Desiccation Crisis
crisis.effectText: Peat bogs and mossy wetlands dry out, and stored peat starts to rot and burn. Remove peat moss and wetland-dependent organisms from chosen tundra and boreal wetland spaces; flip those wetland spaces to dry ground.

organismsGood.example: Deer and small herbivores using new dry patches

effectText: wet places dry up and water-loving life struggles. remove organisms from the board that are in wet biomes.

name: Megaflood
effectText: huge floods wash away soil and life in low areas. remove soil and organism tokens from affected biomes.

name: Multi-year Heat Wave
effectText: The world bakes for many years and heat-sensitive life dies off. Replace or remove cold-loving organisms in hot-stressed biomes.

name: Sudden Cold Snap
effectText: A sudden freeze hits warm regions and tropical life cannot cope. Remove or swap out warm-loving organisms in affected spaces.

name: Ocean Acidification Pulse
effectText: Seawater turns more acidic and shell-building sea life dissolves. Remove or weaken shell-building organisms in affected sea spaces.

name: Harmful Algal Bloom
effectText: Thick green scum covers the water and uses up oxygen. Remove fish and sensitive invertebrates from bloom-marked water spaces.

name: Disease Outbreak
effectText: A new disease sweeps through crowded populations. Remove host species tokens from one biome type in a chosen region.
biomesBad: Any biome with dense host populations

name: Invasive Species Arrival
effectText: A tough new species arrives and pushes out locals. Add an invasive token and replace one matching native organism.

name: Predator Boom
effectText: Predators surge and prey are hit hard. Remove or flip large herbivores or common prey in one chosen region.

name: Wildfire Season
effectText: Fires sweep through and burn non–fire-adapted areas. Remove organisms from 1–2 forest or peatland spaces and mark them as burned.

name: Volcanic Eruption (Regional)
effectText: Ash blankets nearby land and rivers. Remove organisms from one ash-covered land space and one river/coastal space.

name: Ash-Darkened Skies
effectText: Dust and ash block sunlight. For this round, producers in 1–2 chosen regions do not give energy and may be replaced by shade-tolerant types.

name: River Pollution Event
effectText: Chemicals spill into rivers and lakes. Remove or move fish, amphibians, and sensitive invertebrates from two connected freshwater spaces.

name: Habitat Fragmentation
effectText: Big habitats get chopped into small pieces. Remove wide-ranging or specialist organisms and replace them with edge-loving generalists.

name: Oxygen Crash (Local)
effectText: Oxygen disappears from a patch of water. Remove 2 fish or invertebrate tokens from a chosen low-oxygen water space.

recovery.name: New Colonization Wave
recovery.effectText: New hardy species spread into empty spaces. Add new producer or simple organism tokens into recently disturbed biomes.
biomesBad: Old coral reefs with little open space

recovery.name: Nutrient Surge
recovery.effectText: Extra nutrients reach certain waters or floodplains. Add or upgrade producer tokens in one chosen ocean, lake, or floodplain region.

recovery.name: Refugia Discovered
recovery.effectText: Hidden safe spots are found where life can hide. Mark 1–2 spaces as refuges; organisms there ignore the next crisis.

recovery.name: Keystone Species Returns
recovery.effectText: A missing keystone species comes back and stabilizes the web. Add a keystone organism and remove up to two overabundant prey.
biomesBad: Systems where prey drop quickly (short term)
Habitats where competitors of the keystone decline
biomesGood: Forests missing key predators or herbivores

recovery.name: Stabilized Food Web
recovery.effectText: Food webs become more balanced again. Remove one super-dominant species and add a new organism at a different trophic level.
biomesBad: Highly disturbed edges losing chaotic dominance

recovery.name: Climate Settles
recovery.effectText: Extreme heat or cold eases back toward the middle. Let climate-sensitive organisms return to 1–2 spaces that recently lost them.

recovery.name: Oxygen Surge
recovery.effectText: Waters mix and oxygen levels rise again. In one water region, return or add fish and invertebrate tokens that were lost.
biomesBad: Naturally low-oxygen niches for anaerobic microbes

recovery.name: Mutualisms Form
recovery.effectText: New partnerships form between species. Mark one biome as highly cooperative; organisms there are protected from the next crisis.
biomesBad: Old simple systems where non-mutualists lose ground

recovery.name: Migration Wave
recovery.effectText: Whole herds and flocks move to safer places. Move up to two organism tokens from a stressed biome into safer neighboring biomes.

recovery.name: Rapid Regrowth
recovery.effectText: Plants spring back quickly after damage. Turn 1–2 burned or empty spaces into growing forest or grassland and add producer tokens.

extinction.name: Ice Age Crash
extinction.effectText: Shallow sea life crashes as oceans shrink and conditions change fast. Remove 2 marine organism tokens from shallow sea biomes.
biomesBad: Marine (Temperate Shelf and Seas, Temperate Upwelling)

extinction.name: Reef Collapse
extinction.effectText: Reef systems collapse and many shallow sea animals die off. Remove 2 reef-building or shallow marine organism tokens.
biomesBad: Marine (Tropical Coral, Temperate Shelf and Seas)

extinction.name: Great Dying
extinction.effectText: This is the biggest die-off of all. In every major region, remove 2 organism tokens; marine spaces may also lose 1 extra organism if crowded.
biomesBad: Marine (Temperate Shelf and Seas, Tropical Coral)
Forest (Tropical and Subtropical Moist Broadleaf Forests, Boreal Forests and Taiga)
Grassland (Tropical and Subtropical Grasslands, Savannas, and Shrublands)
biomesGood: Desert (Deserts and Xeric Shrublands, Xeric Basins)

organismsBad.example: Trilobites and many corals and brachiopods

extinction.name: Volcanic Warming
extinction.effectText: Volcanic warming and ocean change wipe out many large reptiles and sensitive sea animals. Remove 1 large land organism and 1 marine organism from each affected region.
biomesBad: Marine (Temperate Shelf and Seas, Tropical Coral)
Grassland (Tropical and Subtropical Grasslands, Savannas, and Shrublands)
Forest (Tropical and Subtropical Moist Broadleaf Forests)

extinction.name: Asteroid Impact
extinction.effectText: A giant impact darkens the world and food webs crash. Remove 2 large land organisms and 1 surface-ocean organism from play.
biomesBad: Forest (Tropical and Subtropical Moist Broadleaf Forests, Temperate Broadleaf and Mixed Forests)
Marine (Tropical Coral, Temperate Shelf and Seas)

extinction.name: Peatland Warming Pulse
extinction.effectText: Drained and drying peatlands release huge amounts of stored carbon. In every tundra, boreal forest, and wetland-rich region, remove 2 wetland or moss organisms; then in any 1 other biome type, remove 1 additional producer organism.
biomesGood: Marine (Temperate Shelf and Seas, Temperate Upwelling)

organismsGood.example: Some phytoplankton in newly warm seas

extinction.name: Global Pandemic Spiral
extinction.effectText: A new disease spreads through many animal groups at once. In every biome, remove 1 vertebrate organism and 1 invertebrate organism; then choose any 1 biome and remove 1 extra vertebrate organism there.
biomesBad: Forest (Tropical and Subtropical Moist Broadleaf Forests, Temperate Broadleaf and Mixed Forests)
Grassland (Tropical and Subtropical Grasslands, Savannas, and Shrublands)
Marine (Temperate Shelf and Seas, Tropical Coral)
